articles.title: Formula 1: What are McLaren's papaya rules?
articles.summary: Our Ask Me Anything team explain what 'papaya rules' are for F1 team McLaren.
articles.body:
'Papaya rules' are a code of conduct for McLaren team-mates Oscar Piastri and Lando Norris on the racing track.

The word 'papaya' refers to the colour of the fruit that bears a resemblance to the iconic orange colour of McLaren.

The drivers are often told of 'papaya rules' on radio messages during races when they are battling each other.

It essentially reminds the drivers that they are free to race, but they must keep the battle fair, clean and avoid colliding.

McLaren team principal Andrea Stella said both Piastri and Norris have been involved in creating the code.

It also ensures equality and fairness between the two drivers as McLaren do not have a designated 'number one' driver.

During the 2026 Singapore Grand Prix sprint race, there was a final-lap collision between the McLarens as Norris tried to pass Piastri at Turn Five.

Piastri defended his position but the cars touched and spun in unison, ending the Australian's race while Norris went on to finish eighth.

Stella said: "Very simply, it is unacceptable that two McLarens ever come together on track. This is a fundamental principle of how we go racing, and something both drivers are very well aware of."

The guidelines caused tension between the two drivers as they fought for the drivers' championship - which was won by Norris at the final race of the 2025 season in Abu Dhabi.

McLaren won the 2025 constructors' championship with six races remaining at the Singapore Grand Prix.

What do the rules mean according to the bosses?

McLaren have been urged by some pundits to ditch their papaya rules and reduce their interference in the title battle.

Boss Zak Brown described the code of conduct after the 2024 Italian Grand as "race him hard, race him clean, [but] don't touch".

Team principal Stella told BBC Sport in 2024 that the rules "only have to do with racing with no risks, no contact between the two McLarens and respectfully".

"What's important is that the championship runs within the principles," he said.

"Racing values that we have at McLaren, and that we have created together with our drivers."

articles.title: US Grand Prix result: Kimi Antonelli wins in Austin but has to wait to seal title
articles.summary: Kimi Antonelli needs only two more points to seal his first world title following a dominant victory in the United States Grand Prix.
articles.body:
Kimi Antonelli just missed out on clinching his first world title in a dominant victory in the United States Grand Prix.

The 20-year-old Italian leads Mercedes team-mate George Russell by 123 points after coming home ahead of Red Bull's Max Verstappen and Ferrari's Charles Leclerc.

Antonelli will be crowned champion in Mexico City next weekend as long he does not lose more than 23 points to Russell or more than 24 to Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton.

That means a ninth place would be enough to become champion even if Russell wins the race, and a 10th would be enough if Hamilton is victorious.

If Russell or Hamilton do not win, Antonelli will be champion next Sunday no matter where he finishes.

Antonelli stamped his authority on this race in the same way as he has on the season, and was out of touch even by the first corner as his rivals all battled behind him at the Circuit of the Americas.

Antonelli's sublime victory, his first since the Spanish Grand Prix last month

A race-long squabble between Leclerc and Verstappen for second place

Antonelli took control of the race from the very beginning, an excellent start combined with a gripping scrap through the first lap between Verstappen and Leclerc leaving him more than two seconds clear by the end of the first lap.

Mercedes had chosen the medium tyres for the start, while Leclerc and the Red Bulls of Verstappen and Isack Hadjar started on new softs.

And Antonelli was able to convert that choice into a one-stop race while almost everyone else did two, emphasising his superiority as he finished 16 seconds clear of Leclerc.

The race was also a stamp of approval for the Mercedes upgrade package that was introduced two races ago in Malaysia but initially took them backwards.

Assiduous work ever since has moved it to the point where, while it remains tricky to optimise, it is definitively quicker than the older specification.

"It was the result we needed," Antonelli said. "All this time putting work on the new package and finally seeing the result was very pleasant, perfect strategy to call the one-stop."

As for the title, he said: "I know we are very close. We try to finish on a high and hopefully we can clinch it very soon."

Russell, who started sixth, had a frustrating race. He was given a five-second penalty for leaving the track and gaining an advantage, which dropped him to 10th after his pit stop. He could only make up two places and finished eighth.

Hamilton's fourth place means both he and fellow Briton Russell just about retain a mathematical chance of winning the championship.

The entertainment was provided by Leclerc and Verstappen, initially wheel to wheel and then at a distance as divergent strategies played out.

Leclerc, who started fourth, jumped up to third place behind Verstappen on the exit of the first corner, and then bravely sat it out around the outside of the Red Bull through the high speed Turn Three at the start of the Esses and then dived down the inside into Turn Four.

Verstappen, though, was not finished, and he closed in on Leclerc down the back straight and they fought hard through the switchback series of corners through the stadium section before the Dutchman claimed second place with a dive down the inside of Turn 15.

Verstappen led Leclerc to his first stop on lap 13, Ferrari waiting two laps longer before the Monegasque made his own first stop.

Verstappen went on to the soft tyres and Leclerc the mediums, the Dutchman then switching to mediums when he stopped on lap 31.

But Leclerc's mediums in the second stint allowed him to run eight laps longer than the Red Bull driver.

Leclerc came out 8.5 seconds behind the Dutchman and closed the gap to be on his tail within five laps as Verstappen himself came up behind Lando Norris' McLaren.

They ran nose to tail for two laps before Verstappen passed Norris into Turn One on lap 47, Leclerc following him past later in the lap.

Two laps later, Leclerc picked off Verstappen down the inside of Turn One to secure the second podium position.

Verstappen was grumbling about his car over the radio for much of the race but he had enough to hold off a late charge from Hamilton - on a similar strategy to Leclerc - by one second at the flag.

Norris managed to nurse his tyres to the end with just one stop to beat Hadjar, while the second McLaren of Oscar Piastri fended off Russell for half the race to take seventh.

Racing Bulls' Liam Lawson and Alpine's Pierre Gasly claimed the final points positions in ninth and 10th.

1996 world champion Damon Hill on BBC Radio 5 Live

Kimi Antonelli has an infectious personality. The team love him, he's enjoying everything he's got in F1 and he's very grateful for all the breaks they've given him at Mercedes. But he delivers. He's such a nice kid. It's incredible - 20 years old and he's on the verge of winning his first championship, which I'm sure will be the first of many.

F1 moves south from Texas for the Mexico City Grand Prix next weekend, from 30 October-1 November. It is likely to be the scene of Antonelli's crowning as the sport's youngest world champion.

images.caption: Image caption, Kimi Antonelli has won nine of the 18 races so far this season

articles.title: Un Antonelli con aura de campeón se queda a dos puntos del título
articles.standfirst: Novena victoria, con Russell octavo, en el límite para que Kimi fuera campeón. Alondso 16º y Sainz 18º
articles.summary: Novena victoria, con Russell octavo, en el límite para que Kimi fuera campeón. Alondso 16º y Sainz 18º
articles.body: Un Kimi Antonelli dominador, imperturbable e inalcanzable para cualquier rival se ha llevado la novena victoria del año en el GP de Estados Unidos, quizá la más brillante de una temporada su llevará su nombre para siempre. El italiano le sacó 7 segundos a Russell en la qualy del sábado y nada menos que 54 segundos en la carrera a su compañero con el mismo coche. Si hubiera terminado un puesto más abajo del octavo final logrado por el inglés, el astro italiano sería ahora campeón del mundo, el más joven de la historia con sólo 20 años. Lo certificará en México en siete días, si acaba entre los nueve primeros. Lo tiene en el bolsillo. Decía Kimi en Singapur que no quería "ganar de cualquier manera", sino en todo lo alto y sus deseos se han materializado. Es uno de los campeones más brillantes y dominadores de la historia y los 123 puntos que le saca a un gran piloto como Russell, a falta de cinco pruebas para el final dan idea y la dimensión de su hazaña. Italia tendrá un nuevo campeón del mundo 73 años después de Alberto Ascari en 1953, palabras mayores. Es algo que devuelve al país transalpino a la cabeza del deporte mundial, después de los sinsabores de la azzurra en el fútbol. Fernando Alonso fue tocado por Albon en la salida y su coche quedó dañado. Además de caer cinco posiciones, hasta el 17º, todo se le hizo cuesta arriba. Quizá con otra salida hubiera estado cerca de puntuar de nuevo, pero pese a la remontada, con la que llegó a estar 10 en algún momento, hubo de ceder y cambiar el morro roto al final de la prueba. Para Carlos Sainz fue incluso peor, porque uno de los RB le encerró contra el muro en la salida y raspó la pared con el exterior de su ala delantera. Estaba 16º, pero sin ritmo alguno y con un monoplaza mermado. Lo de Williams va a ser un sufrimiento hasta el final del año. Tiempos, cortesía de formula-timer.com. Un Antonelli perfecto mantenía el liderato y Max se quedaba un tanto clavado. Leclerc la pasaba en el primer sector, pero el holandés le recuperaba plaza entes de pasar por meta. Alonso caía al 17º tras una mala primera vuelta y Sainz subía al 15º. En la vuelta 3 Max estaba a 2,2 segundos de Kimi y quedaba toda la carrera. Fernando ganaba el 16º, con más ritmo que el Williams de Carlos. T Russell estaba investigado por ganar ventaja tras salirse de la pista. Era sexto el compañero de Antonelli. A Carlos le había cerrado uno de los RB en la salida contra el muro, en una acción más que revisable. Su ala delantera estaba tocada y perdía 20 puntos de carga aerodinámica. A Russell le caían cinco segundos de penalización en la vuelta 9 y la tendría que cumplir en su parada. El Mundial de Antonelli no estaba tan lejos. Después de 9 vueltas tras la estela del Williams lograba pasarle para ir en pos de Bearman y seguir la escalada. Verstappen paraba en la vuelta 14º y colocaba el blando de nuevo. No parecía lo más acertado y Kimi seguía primero. Tras la parada de Bearman (V14), Alonso era 14º y estaba a 5,9 segundos de Hulkenberg. Los Ferrari también entraban en boxes y Hadjar se quedaba segundo. Max era quinto a 17 segundos de KImi en la vuelta 18. Verstappen pasaba a Russell en la vuelta 19 y era cuarto, a 16 seg de Kimi. George entraba en la vuelta 23 y Kimi era líder sólido con 12 segundos sobre Hadjar yb 12,7 sobre Max con una parada. El holandés pasaba a su compañero en esa vuelta. Alonso era 12º sin haber parado todavía. Montaba el duro y pretendía ir hasta el final con ese juego de neumáticos. Alonso subía al décimo sin parar aún. Alonso paraba en la vuelta 30 para su única parada y colocaba el compuesto medio. Regresaba 14º y los puntos estaban a su alcance. Colocaba el medio para ir hasta el final y regresaba quinto, a 19 segundos de Antonelli. Todo estaba decidido. Fernando estaba 14º, a 3 segundos de Hulkenberg y llegar a los puntos parecía muy complicado. Alonso paraba de nuevo en la vuelta 44 para cambiar el morro dañado y regresaba 17º. Antonelli tenía la victoria en el bolsillo y Norris aguantaba a Verstappen en la parte final. Leclerc buscaba el segundo. En la vuelta 47 y con Leclerc a la espalda, Verstappen pasó con una apurada antológica y tomó el segundo. Charles adelantaba a Lando y se iba a por el Red Bull. Leclerc, mucho más veloz, pasó a Max en la vuelta 50 y el ganador era Antonelli, segundo el monegasco de Ferrari y tercero Verstappen.

articles.title: NASCAR Talladega Wreck Recap: Biggest Crashes, Drivers Involved and Championship Fallout
articles.summary: Talladega's YellaWood 500 featured multiple major crashes that devastated championship contenders. Here's a breakdown of the wrecks, drivers involved and the...
articles.body:
Sunday's YellaWood 500 at Talladega Superspeedway delivered exactly what NASCAR's championship contenders feared: wrecks, ruined afternoons and a major shake-up in the Chase standings.

Kyle Larson somehow avoided the worst of the trouble, winning and leaving Alabama with a 73-point championship lead. Several of his closest rivals weren't nearly as fortunate.

From an early setback for Christopher Bell to a frightening late crash involving Joey Logano and Riley Herbst, here's how the biggest incidents unfolded.

Christopher Bell's Championship Hopes Take an Early Hit

Bell entered Talladega just five points behind Larson. His afternoon unraveled before the first stage was over.

While leading a group of Toyotas toward pit road, Bell lost control of his No. 20 Toyota and struck the inside wall. The impact caused significant damage, and repeated tire problems compounded the setback.

A penalty for too many crew members over the wall only made matters worse.

Bell finished 35th, 12 laps down, and fell to third in the championship standings, 74 points behind Larson.

The Big One Collects Eight Championship Contenders

Talladega's first major multicar crash erupted on the backstretch during Stage 2.

Ryan Blaney was running near teammate Joey Logano when the outside lane became unsettled. Contact involving Blaney and Bubba Wallace triggered a chain reaction that swept up 12 cars.

Eight Chase drivers were involved: Blaney, Wallace, Denny Hamlin, Tyler Reddick, Ty Gibbs, Ryan Preece, Chase Elliott and Daniel Suarez.

Ross Chastain, Noah Gragson, John Hunter Nemechek and Gray Gaulding were also caught in the accident.

Blaney, Reddick and Elliott suffered particularly costly finishes, placing 38th, 37th and 36th, respectively. Hamlin continued despite front-end damage and ultimately finished eighth.

Joey Logano Flips in Terrifying Late-Race Crash

With five laps remaining, another massive wreck brought the race to a halt.

Logano was racing near the front when contact in the outside lane sent his No. 22 Ford into Chase Briscoe's Toyota. Logano's car went airborne and landed upside down.

The accident collected numerous drivers, including Carson Hocevar, Austin Cindric, Chris Buescher, Connor Zilisch, Erik Jones, Daniel Suarez and AJ Allmendinger.

Herbst suffered one of the hardest impacts of the afternoon when his No. 35 Toyota slammed into the inside SAFER barrier.

The race was red-flagged for approximately 13 minutes as safety workers responded and crews cleared the track.

Logano climbed from his car under his own power. Herbst also exited his vehicle, and NASCAR later confirmed both drivers had been evaluated and released from the infield care center.

Logano, who had won Stage 2 and led 23 laps, finished 34th. Briscoe finished 33rd, while Cindric placed 27th.

Talladega's Wrecks Reshape the NASCAR Championship Battle

The damage extended well beyond Sunday's finishing order.

Larson escaped with the victory, beating William Byron by 0.041 seconds in overtime. Meanwhile, Bell, Briscoe, Logano and Blaney all endured finishes outside the top 30.

Hamlin moved into second in the standings, 73 points behind Larson, with Bell third at 74 points back.

With Martinsville and Homestead remaining, the Chase looks dramatically different than it did when the field arrived at Talladega.

For Larson, surviving the chaos proved just as valuable as winning the race .

articles.title: Kimi Antonelli F1 title permutations: How Mercedes driver can win 2026 Formula 1 Drivers' Championship at Mexico City GP on Sunday
articles.summary: How can Kimi Antonelli become the youngest champion in Formula 1 history this Sunday at the Mexico City Grand Prix? Watch every session of the Mexico City GP from this Friday, live on Sky Sports F1
articles.body:
Antonelli won the United States Grand Prix in Austin to move 123 points clear of his Mercedes team-mate and nearest challenger George Russell, and 124 points ahead of Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton.

Red Bull's Max Verstappen, Ferrari's Charles Leclerc and McLaren's Lando Norris were officially knocked out of championship contention, leaving Russell and Hamilton as the only drivers who can technically prevent Antonelli from becoming the sport's youngest ever world champion at 20 years old.

In reality, Russell and Hamilton's chances are only technical, as one of them would need to win all five remaining races and for Antonelli to fail to score two points.

How Antonelli can win the 2026 F1 title at the Mexico City GP

There will be four scheduled races left - Brazil, Las Vegas, Qatar and Abu Dhabi - after the Mexico City Grand Prix takes place this Sunday and a maximum of 100 points left to play for.

To win the title in Austin, Antonelli simply needs to score two points, or not be outscored by Russell by 23 points and Hamilton by 24 points.

The permutations for Antonelli to become champion in Mexico City are:

Russell and Hamilton fail to win the race

When can Mercedes clinch the Constructors' Championship?

Mercedes will also have a first mathematical chance to clinch the Constructors' Championship in Mexico - but securing that title next time out is a very tall order.

They lead Ferrari by 133 points in the standings and there will be 172 points left to play for after this Sunday's race.

To become champions in Mexico, they would need to outscore Ferrari by 39 points. This would require Antonelli or Russell winning the Grand Prix, with the other driver in second or third, plus a disastrous race for both Ferrari drivers.

The Silver Arrows' first realistic chance to wrap things up will therefore likely come at next week's Sao Paulo Grand Prix when they would only need to finish the Interlagos event 129 points ahead, four fewer than now.

However, Ferrari have outscored them at each of the last three race weekends.

articles.title: Fernando Alonso criticises Alex Albon and says 'quality of drivers is very low' in bottom third of F1 field at United States GP
articles.summary: Aston Martin's Fernando Alonso and Williams' Alex Albon collided on the opening lap of the United States Grand Prix; Alonso criticised Albon and hit out at other drivers in the midfield; watch every session of the Mexico City GP from Friday, live on Sky Sports F1
articles.body:
Albon tried to overtake Alonso for 12th place into the Turn 11 hairpin on the opening lap, but went into the side of the Aston Martin driver, damaging both cars.

Neither driver received a penalty and both were able to continue with Alonso finishing 16th and Albon in 17th in Austin.

"Albon forgot Turn 11 was there and he had to turn left," said Alonso.

"We need to get better and start a little bit higher up because the bottom third of the grid, the quality of the drivers is very low at the moment."

Alonso qualified 12th, his joint-best Saturday result of the season, and thinks points were on the cards if not for the damage, which cost him around half a second per lap.

"It was the best race by far of the year for us in terms of competitiveness. Good tyre management. We got a lot of damage on Lap 1 with the Albon incident," he said.

"Despite that, the car was still competitive. We had a P9 or P10 on merit. The best and strongest race of the year but ruined in the first lap with the Turn 11 incident."

Albon felt he did not need need to apologise for the collision with Alonso as Esteban Ocon was on the outside of the Spaniard and also played a role in the incident.

"It's racing. I think there was a car on his outside that squeezed [him]. I was side by side with him the whole way into the corner. It's hard to disappear," said the Williams driver.

"I thought we had some good racing. We had a second go at it later in the race. I enjoyed it at least. I hope he feels the same way on the second half. It was good fun."

articles.title: US Grand Prix: Kimi Antonelli delivers 'the race of a champion who isn't the champion yet'
articles.summary: Kimi Antonelli's Austin win was "the best he has delivered", according to Mercedes boss Toto Wolff, even if it wasn't quite enough to give him the title.
articles.body:
The race that took Kimi Antonelli to the brink of a record-breaking world championship was, in the words of his Mercedes team boss Toto Wolff, "the best he has delivered so far" and "the race of a champion who isn't the champion yet".

The 20-year-old Italian's victory in the United States Grand Prix puts him in an impregnable position.

Antonelli is so far ahead in the points that the only way he could not win the title in Mexico City next weekend is if either his team-mate George Russell or Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton win the race. Even then, Antonelli will guarantee the title if he finishes ninth, or 10th if it's Hamilton.

He arrived here thanks to one of the most dominant victories of the season, in a car in which Russell could finish only eighth, albeit hampered by a five-second penalty.

While Russell was toiling and failing to pass McLaren's Oscar Piastri, Antonelli was operating on another level entirely, as he has so often this season.

"Exceptional," Wolff said, "and I think he's outperformed the car."

Antonelli wins in US but has to wait to secure title

Antonelli superb and Leclerc close to perfect - driver ratings

Antonelli came to Austin already in a strong position in the championship, knowing he would clinch the title if he won with Russell finishing lower than eighth and Hamilton lower than fourth.

He achieved his part of the bargain but Russell and Hamilton did just enough to keep things alive until this coming weekend. Russell was eighth and Hamilton fourth.

Some drivers tighten up when they get this close to achieving their lifetime's ambition. Not Antonelli. He said he was going to treat this like any other weekend, but it wasn't just talk. It's exactly what he did.

"He comes in," Wolff told BBC Sport after the race, in a conversation after finishing his official news conference, "sits on my chair, feet up, and keeps chatting away and saying: 'This is so funny. I'm not thinking about the championship at all.' And in a kind of youngish excitement, almost like it's surreal. And that's why it's not so important."

Did Wolff think that was because Antonelli's lead was so large that he had no need to feel any pressure, or was it innate?

"The advantage helps," he said. "But it's also innate in him and I don't think that it's something to be trained for. He's not over-thinking it."

Wolff's claim about this being Antonelli's best performance so far might surprise anyone who watched him win his home grand prix at Monza from 19th on the grid.

When this was pointed out, Wolff replied: "My problem is that I don't remember past races. So now you're saying Monza was actually also pretty good, obviously with the advantage of the home crowd and seeing all these tifosi that were a little bit confused, wearing red, and an Italian with the Mercedes outfit up on the podium. And I think we're going to see more Kimi caps, Mercedes caps next year.

"So both of them were pretty good. But the headline that this is the best we can keep."

Antonelli agreed. "Monza, we clearly had the fastest car," he said. "We were just super quick, so of course it was incredibly special coming from the back. But it was also a track where it was relatively easy to overtake, and we were so quick.

"Definitely, Monza was a super-special one, and one that I will remember forever. But this one probably, in terms of execution, was better, because the way we built up and the way we built the performance throughout the weekend was very good."

Mercedes went to Austin with both cars in the new upgraded specification that had proved unconvincing, to say the least, when it made its debut in Malaysia two races ago.

There, Wolff said he thought it had made the car 0.3secs per lap slower. The team split the cars in Singapore to try to understand the package better, and then used it on both cars in Austin. Antonelli stuck it on pole and dominated the race. Russell's performance looked more like the one the car produced in Malaysia.

"The update we put on the car is difficult to operate," Wolff said. "And Kimi landed it.

"Maybe it's a bit harsh to say but I think his driving style just glues with the car. We saw that in qualifying yesterday where on his last lap he could have been another 0.15-0.2 secs up. And on the other side George just struggled so much. And I believe this is because the operational window of the car is so difficult."

When Antonelli clinches the title, he will become the first Italian to do so since Alberto Ascari in 1953. It's a remarkable statistic for a country which is so engrained in the sport, and it certainly resonates with his compatriots.

McLaren team principal Andrea Stella said: "As an Italian, wow, we need to go back to Ascari, the names that they created the inspiration for all of us. To see an Italian achieving this level of performance and results in Formula 1, that's particularly thrilling, as an Italian person in motorsport."

Stella's answer continued into an area that begins to explain the way in which he has proved so superior to Russell this year.

"Going more into the technical, and specifically this season, Kimi is a very interesting one to look at, because he pretty much attacks all the times," Stella said.

"You see how often he's just going off track, and you see his onboard (camera), he's pretty aggressive. But at the same time, this seems to be not only kind of an aggressive driving, or an attacking driving, but effective.

"And if we think how much we talk in these media sessions about the cars being difficult to drive consistently fast, it should be recognised how much he's been able to harness his driving style with what is required of the cars.

"But at the same time, almost contradicting what I'm saying, when is the time to bring home the result, he's been able to do it.

"So he's the deserving leader of this championship. He's writing an important piece of history for motorsport, because once he achieves the championship, he will be the youngest."

Antonelli will beat by more than three years the previous record for youngest winner of the championship, Sebastian Vettel in 2010.

As with the title itself, he is aware of the forthcoming achievement, but not letting it affect him.

"I'm going to approach it with the same mindset," he said. "Just trying to have as much fun as possible, trying to hopefully fight for another win.

"It would be best to finish on a high, and that's the goal. But I'm just going to try to enjoy the rest of the season from now on."

articles.title: United States Grand Prix: Harry Benjamin's driver ratings as Kimi Antonelli wins in Austin
articles.summary: BBC Radio 5 Live F1 commentator Harry Benjamin rates how the drivers performed during the United States Grand Prix.
articles.body:
Championship leader Kimi Antonelli sealed his ninth victory of the season with victory at the United States Grand Prix in Austin.

Ferrari's Charles Leclerc was second and Red Bull's Max Verstappen third.

Mercedes' Antonelli, 20, can become the youngest world champion in Formula 1 history if he finishes ninth or higher at the Mexico City Grand Prix next weekend.

Here are my ratings for how the drivers performed across the whole weekend in Texas.

A superb weekend under the added pressure of having his first opportunity to seal the championship. Produced an outstanding lap for pole and then controlled the race beautifully, making the one-stop work while many around him needed two.

Very close to a perfect weekend himself. Fastest in both Friday practice sessions, qualified fourth and then raced brilliantly in his Ferrari to second, including late passes on Lando Norris and Max Verstappen.

Quick all weekend and put the Red Bull on the front row, but the poor start immediately made his race more difficult. Recovered well despite problems with the car and still came away with a sixth consecutive podium.

Another strong weekend but behind team-mate Leclerc for the majority of it. Fastest in final practice, only narrowly behind Leclerc in qualifying and fought his way back to fourth after Ferrari committed to the two-stop strategy.

Recovered well from eighth on the grid but qualifying should have been better as his quickest Q3 lap was deleted for track limits. McLaren's decision to leave him out on ageing tyres cost him late on, so fifth was not entirely of his own making.

An excellent turnaround after struggling badly with the Red Bull during practice. Qualified a superb third, ran strongly in the race and eventually finished sixth despite throttle mapping problems and moving aside for team-mate Verstappen.

A fairly subdued weekend by the McLaren man's standards. Seventh in qualifying and seventh in the race, although the first-lap battle with George Russell went against him and the stewards decided the Mercedes driver was at fault.

A disappointing weekend given what the other Mercedes achieved. Admitted both of his Q3 laps were poor and then picked up a five-second time penalty for leaving the track and gaining an advantage in his battle with Piastri, eventually finishing eighth.

Another quietly excellent weekend from Lawson. Racing Bulls sacrificed a proper Q3 attempt to preserve tyres for Sunday and he converted ninth on the grid into ninth at the finish to score again.

Probably extracted just about everything available from the Alpine. Missed Q3 but fought his way back into the points after an early dice with Haas' Oliver Bearman.

Antonelli wins in US but has to wait to secure title

Antonelli delivers 'the race of a champion who isn't the champion yet'

Another solid if unspectacular weekend for the Audi driver. Just missed Q3 and spent Sunday on the fringes of the points before eventually finishing 11th.

Reaching Q3 was an excellent effort after admitting team-mate Lawson had been quicker than him for much of the weekend. A power-unit penalty dropped him from ninth to 14th on the grid and he recovered a couple of positions to 12th.

A much better weekend than 13th suggests. Produced what he described as one of his best qualifying laps before helping team-mate Hulkenberg with a tow, then recovered from 21st on the grid after an enormous power-unit penalty.

Out in Q1 and again lacked the pace team-mate Bearman had shown earlier in the weekend. Gained places at the start and Haas eventually prioritised his undamaged car, but 14th was all he could manage.

Started from the pit lane after Aston Martin made changes to the car and fitted additional power unit components, so 15th represented a reasonable recovery. Beat team-mate Fernando Alonso to the flag after a weekend where neither car looked particularly competitive.

Getting the Aston Martin into Q2 was encouraging and penalties initially promoted him to 12th on the grid. But he went backwards on Sunday and contact with Williams' Alex Albon didn't help as he eventually finished behind Stroll after a slow pit stop.

Williams knew this circuit would expose the weaknesses of their car and that proved to be the case. Qualified behind team-mate Carlos Sainz but at least he recovered to lead the team home after an eventful opening part of the race.

A mistake late in his final qualifying lap contributed to a Q1 exit on a weekend when Williams were already struggling badly. Finished behind Albon and never looked capable of rescuing points from a difficult weekend.

Beat team-mate Valtteri Bottas in qualifying despite suffering an energy-recovery issue on his final lap. But Cadillac simply didn't have competitive pace at their home race, and P19 was a fairly anonymous result.

Qualified last before eventually retiring late enough to trigger the final virtual safety car. There wasn't much evidence across the weekend that Cadillac had the performance to achieve anything significant.

Qualified 14th but a 10-place power-unit penalty left the Alpine driver effectively starting from the back. His retirement meant there was little opportunity to turn the weekend around.

There had been real promise after he led Haas throughout Friday and initially looked quick enough for 13th in qualifying before losing his lap to track limits. Sunday unravelled with contact, a penalty and damage before he eventually retired.

articles.body: COIMBATORE: A last-corner touring-car clash, a 0.004-second battle for fourth in the Novice F1300 race and a rain-disrupted LGB F4 finale ensured a dramatic finish to the opening round of the CTR-JK Tyre FMSCI Indian National Car Racing Championship 2026 in Coimbatore on Sunday.In LGB Formula 4, Meco Racing’s Dhruvh Goswami starred in the opening race of the day, surviving repeated safety-car periods and a tense final-lap battle to win by 0.356 seconds. After an extra formation lap and early issues for Ahura Racing, Goswami fought the Dark Don Racing drivers and retook the lead with a bold outside move on Mehul Agarwal. Arya Singh finished third, while rookie Ashwin Kumar KP impressed in eighth overall.The second race was hit by heavy rain and poor visibility, starting behind the safety car before being red-flagged and classified after nine laps. Balaprasath won from pole by 0.392 seconds over teammate Agarwal, with Raghul Rangasamy third.In the Royal Enfield Continental GT Cup Pro class, Bengaluru’s Anish Shetty charged from fifth to victory, beating Navaneeth Kumar by 4.091 seconds and setting a 1:15.648 fastest lap.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Horarios del GP de México de Fórmula 1: fechas y dónde ver en TV a Fernando Alonso y Carlos Sainz en Ciudad de México
articles.standfirst: Kimi tendrá una oportunidad de oro para cerrar el título en el Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez
articles.summary: Kimi tendrá una oportunidad de oro para cerrar el título en el Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez
articles.body: El Mundial de Fórmula 1 regresa a la casa de 'Checo' Pérez con el mexicano en activo otra vez, aunque muy probablemente, y según los rumores, volverá a despedirse del Mundial frente a su gente. No obstante, Pérez no tendrá toda la atención que querría, pues Antonelli se proclamará Campeón del Mundo, siempre y cuando termine dentro de los 9 primeros que, viendo cómo ha sido su temporada, lo tiene todo de cara para cerrar el segundo 'Match Ball'. Un 4º puesto de Hamilton y un 8º de Russell en el Gran premio de Estados Unidos le arrebataron al italiano la posibilidad de alzarse con el título en Austin. El líder hizo sus deberes y, además de firmar la 'pole' el sábado, se llevó la victoria en tierras americanas. Sin embargo, Hamilton debía quedar 5º o peor y Russell 9º o peor para que Antonelli pudiera grabar su nombre en el trofeo de Campeones. Aun así, esta victoria le da un gran margen y seguridad de cerrar el Mundial la próxima semana en México, siempre y cuando no se cancelen las dos últimas citas en Qatar y Abu Dhabi, lo cual ya habría dado el campeonato al italiano tras Singapur. De nuevo, un fin de semana complicado es el que han vivido Fernando Alonso y Carlos Sainz. Su Aston Martin y Williams no consiguen mejorar lo más mínimo ni mantenerse firmes en los pequeños pasos que puedan llegar a dar, haciendo de cada fon de semana un desastre. En este caso, y a pesar de que se vieron beneficiados por las sanciones por cambio en su Unidad de Potencia a Lindblad, Bortoleto y Colapinto, la mala fortuna les volvió a mirar de frente e incidentes durante la carrera les privaron de firmar mejores posiciones, acabando 16º el asturiano y 18º el madrileño. 1º. Kimi Antonelli (MERCEDES) 365p. 2º. George Russell (MERCEDES) 242p. 3º. Lewis Hamilton (FERRARI) 241p. 4º. Max Verstappen (RED BULL) 236p. 5º. Charles Leclerc (FERRARI) 233p. Como es habitual, el Gran Premio de México de Fórmula 1 2026 se podrá ver en directo por televisión a través de DAZN F1 y en Movistar+. También tienes la opción de seguir todo lo que suceda en la carrera en el circuito Hermanos Rodríguez a través de los directos de MARCA.com y la transmisión de la carrera en Radio MARCA. articles.title: A Antonelli le vale un noveno: "Y beberemos tequila en México"
articles.standfirst: El italiano venció de forma brillante en Austin y amarra por completo el Campeonato del Mundo. Suma 9 victorias y 15 podios
articles.summary: El italiano venció de forma brillante en Austin y amarra por completo el Campeonato del Mundo. Suma 9 victorias y 15 podios
articles.body: Andrea Kimi Antonelli se sigue acercando al título mundial. Tras firmar una pole que parecía imposible en el sábado del Gran Premio de los Estados Unidos, el italiano completó la exhibición con un triunfo sin discusión en la cita de Austin que le acerca a lo que sería una corona histórica en la Fórmula 1. La más joven de todos los tiempos y también una de las más inesperadas dado que sólo es su segunda temporada en la F1 y venía de un 2025 con muchos problemas. Pero en la nueva reglamentación todo cambió. Y Antonelli, que presenta unos grandes guarismos de nueve victorias, 15 podios y siete poles, sigue demostrando que no teme a ese momento de la coronación. "El equipo sólo me dice que me divierta", repitió durante todo el fin de semana de Austin y en pista se ejemplificó con la primera nlaza que le deja a tiro de campeonato en México o Brasil, las dos citas que cerrarán el triplete. "Si es en México, beberemos tequila. Si es en Interlagos, mojito o algo así...", bromeaba su jefe, Toto Wolff. Pero son realistas, obviamente. "Es excepcional lo que está haciendo, increíble. Me dice que no piensa en el Mundial y que sólo quiere disfrutar, es lo correcto", añadió. Antonelli refrendó que el de Austin también sería un buen fin de semana cuando logró una pole en unas condiciones climáticas y de adherencia variables. Verstappen falló y abrió el camino al italiano. Después se encontraron en la primera curva de carrera y el italiano salió, de nuevo, vencedor de ese envite clave. Ya había ocurrido anteriormente en Mónaco y Spa, con dos ocasiones en las que el líder del Mundial mantuvo su puesto y puso la directa a dos de sus triunfos en el presente campeonato. En Texas ni eso, pues Max no pudo atacar. Ahora la F1 queda con un panorama mucho más claro. Si el título era difícil en Austin y necesitaba un noveno de Russell (fue octavo) y sexto de Hamilton (terminó cuatro), en México es más probable pues aterrizará con 123 puntos de los 125 que quedarán en disputa... si no se cancela nada entre Qatar y Abu Dhabi. En otras palabras, necesita finalizar la cita del Hermanos Rodríguez con dos unidades más de renta. Se lo daría un noveno en la próxima carrera. Algo que ha logrado todo el curso a excepción de las citas con problemas mecánicos en Barcelona y Silverstone. En las dos tenía el podio asegurado. Y todos saben que puede llegar. "Me encanta ver a un piloto tan joven pelear por el título, lo está haciendo realmente bien", comentó Verstappen sobre el italiano. Que quiere añadir el título a una lista de logros que no deja de crecer. Ya ha sido el más joven con un Grand Slam, el primero en lograr sus tres primeras victorias con tres carreras ganadas seguidas... Todo apunta a Kimi. Y en Austin se acercó más que nunca.
